title: Lesson 2 - Object-Permission Scenarios and Mass-Assign / License-Based Patterns
description: Given a scenario, recommend the right level of object permissions needed to provide the appropriate access to a set of users, including mass-assignment and license-aware patterns.

questions.question: An admin must grant 400 sales users Edit access to a custom object, but only a handful of execs should see it at all. What is the cleanest approach?
options: Add Edit to the sales profile for everyone
Create a permission set granting Edit, put it in a group, and dynamically assign the group to sales users
Create a separate profile for each exec
Make the custom object's OWD Public Read/Write
questions.explanation: A permission set + group + dynamic assignment scales to 400 users without bloating the profile or changing sharing. Editing the shared profile grants it to non-sales users too, and OWD changes affect everyone.

questions.question: A permission set exists to grant access to a paid managed-package object, but assigning it to a user produces a license error. What is the most likely cause?
options: The user's profile has the object on page layout
The permission set is qualified for a license the user does not have
The profile already grants View All
questions.explanation: Managed-package object permissions are license-gated; if the permission set is tied to a license the user lacks, assignment fails. The other choices do not cause a license error.

questions.question: Which is the recommended pattern for scaling a permission grant to a large, frequently-changing user population?
options: Edit the standard profile each time a new hire starts
Create a permission set group and use dynamic assignment rules on user attributes
Manually assign individual permission sets to each user
Set the object OWD to Public Read Only
questions.explanation: Dynamic assignment on a permission set group automatically covers joiners/leavers by filter criteria, the most scalable and least manual pattern.
